prompt: Compare every student with every other student to find matching birthdays.
tells: every student with every other student
why: Each student is compared with every other student, so the work is about n times n. Checking all pairs is O(n²).
trap: A set would make it linear, but that isn't what's described.

prompt: Doubling the guests makes the number of handshakes about four times as big.
why: With twice the guests, each person shakes about twice as many hands, so the total grows four times. Double the input, four times the work, is O(n²).

prompt: A loop inside a loop, both over the whole list.
why: For each item, the inner loop goes over every item again, giving n times n steps. Nested loops over the same list are O(n²).
trap: Two loops one after the other would still be linear.

prompt: Bubble sort keeps sweeping the list, swapping neighbours, until no swaps are left.
why: Each sweep walks the whole list, and it can take up to n sweeps. n sweeps of n items is O(n²).
trap: One sweep is linear; many sweeps aren't.

prompt: Check every pair of photos to find duplicates.
why: Every photo is compared with every other photo to spot duplicates. Checking all pairs grows as n squared, O(n²).
trap: Pairs grow much faster than photos.

prompt: With 1,000 items the program takes 1 second; with 10,000 it takes about 100 seconds.
why: Ten times the data took a hundred times as long, which is ten squared. Time that grows with the square of the size is O(n²).
